Extended workflow

This is a complete example you can copy into an R script or Quarto document and run. It uses a Word document with an image, a table, a citation and four placeholders, and shows a child Quarto file, a chunk, an inline value and a plain value side by side.

If you haven’t already, read vignette("knittogether") first. It explains the terms used here and how to work back and forth with Word.

Example files

Normally your colleague would give you the Word document. So the example can run anywhere, the code below creates one, along with an image, a bibliography and a child Quarto file. Everything goes into a temporary folder, which is why the paths below are wrapped in file.path(temp_dir, ...). You won’t need that in your own work.

Code to create the example files

create_base_files() can also make a PowerPoint version with output = "pptx". That needs Pandoc 3.8.3 or later.

Code
library(pandoc)
library(withr)
# Use a temporary working directory for this vignette
temp_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "knittogether_vignette_workflow")
dir.create(temp_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Recreates the starting files, so the example can be run again from scratch
create_base_files <- function(output = "docx", child_qmd = TRUE, image = TRUE, bib = TRUE, render = TRUE) {

  if (child_qmd) {
  child_qmd <- paste(
    "## Content from a child qmd",
    "",
    "```{r}",
    "plot(1, 1)",
    "```",
    "",
    "The addition of 1 and 1 is `r 1+1`.",
    "",
    sep = "\n")

  writeLines(child_qmd, file.path(temp_dir, "child_example.qmd"))
  }

  if (image) {
  png(file.path(temp_dir, "image.png"), width = 600, height = 400)
  x <- 1:10
  plot(x, x^2, type = "b", col = "blue", pch = 19,
       main = "Example Image Created in R", xlab = "X values", ylab = "Y values (squared)")
  dev.off()
  }

  if (bib) {
  bib <- ("@book{roseRosesStrategyPreventive2008,
          title = {Rose's {{Strategy}} of {{Preventive Medicine}}},
          author = {Rose, Geoffrey},
          year = 2008,
          month = jan,
          publisher = {OUP Oxford},
          abstract = {},
          isbn = {978-0-19-101559-5}
          }"
          )

    writeLines(bib, file.path(temp_dir, "example.bib"))
  }

  if (output == "docx") {
  example_qmd <- r"(
---
title: "Example Word Document"
subtitle: "This document is used as a knittogether example"
format: docx
---

# Introduction

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.[@roseRosesStrategyPreventive2008]

![Fig 1. A plot](image.png){fig-alt="A image"}

## More info

  -   Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.
  -   Quisque faucibus ex sapien vitae pellentesque sem placerat.
  -   Tempus leo eu aenean sed diam urna tempor.

# Main content

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit. placeholder_total.

  1.  Quisque faucibus ex sapien vitae pellentesque sem placerat.
      1.  In id cursus mi pretium tellus duis convallis.
  2.  Tempus leo eu aenean sed diam urna tempor.

| Col1 | Col2 | Col3 |
|------|------|------|
| A    | 1    | 4    |
| B    | 2    | 5    |
| C    | 3    | 6    |

: Table 1. This is a table

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.

placeholder_childqmd

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.

placeholder_1x1plot

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.

The number of rows in the data set is placeholder_mtcarsrows.
)"

  writeLines(example_qmd, file.path(temp_dir, "example.qmd"))

  if (render) {
    pandoc::pandoc_run(c(file.path(temp_dir, "example.qmd"), "-f",
                         "markdown", "-o", file.path(temp_dir, "example.docx")))
    }
  } else if (output == "pptx") {
    example_qmd <- r"(
---
title: "Example PowerPoint Presentation"
subtitle: "This presentation is used as a knittogether example"
format: pptx
---

# Introduction

## Background

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.

# Main Content

## Dinner

  -   Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.
  -   Quisque faucibus ex sapien vitae pellentesque sem placerat.
  -   Tempus leo eu aenean sed diam urna tempor.

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit. placeholder_total.

  1.  Quisque faucibus ex sapien vitae pellentesque sem placerat.
      1.  In id cursus mi pretium tellus duis convallis.
  2.  Tempus leo eu aenean sed diam urna tempor.

## A plot

placeholder_1x1plot

)"

  writeLines(example_qmd, file.path(temp_dir, "example.qmd"))

    if (render) {
      pandoc::pandoc_run(c(file.path(temp_dir, "example.qmd"), "-f",
                           "markdown", "-o", file.path(temp_dir, "example.pptx")))
      }
  }
}

create_base_files(output = "docx")

Convert

Turn the Word document into Markdown. The image goes into a media/ folder inside media_base_dir.

knittogether::convert_markdown(
  input_file = file.path(temp_dir, "example.docx"),
  markdown_file = file.path(temp_dir, "example.md"),
  media_base_dir = file.path(temp_dir, "workflow")
)

This document is simple, so the default settings are fine. Tables with long text or line breaks inside cells may convert better as GitHub-flavoured Markdown, which you can ask for with pandoc_args = "-t gfm". For full control over Pandoc, call pandoc::pandoc_run() yourself. Other Markdown flavours can leave extra escaping behind, which clean_markdown() then needs to tidy up.

Clean 

knittogether::clean_markdown(
  markdown_file = file.path(temp_dir, "example.md"),
  placeholder_prefix = "placeholder_",
  heading_offset = TRUE,
  clean_citations = TRUE
)

heading_offset = TRUE moves each heading down a level, so the Word “Heading 1” sections don’t compete with the page title in HTML. clean_citations = TRUE removes the extra \ that Pandoc puts in front of citation brackets.

Define the content

There are four placeholders in the document, each filled in a different way:

# A chunk that comes from a separate Quarto file
child <- knittogether::define_content(
  description = "A plot in a child qmd",
  placeholder_id = "childqmd",
  output_mode = "chunk",
  content = "{{< include child_example.qmd >}}",
  content_type = "plot",
  chunk_options = list(engine = "r", as_child = TRUE,
                       child_dir = "children", echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7))

# A chunk written here
plot <- knittogether::define_content(
  description = "A plot",
  placeholder_id = "1x1plot",
  output_mode = "chunk",
  content = { plot(1, 1) },
  content_type = "plot",
  chunk_options = list(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 7))

# An inline value, worked out when the document renders
inline <- knittogether::define_content(
  description = "Number of rows in mtcars",
  placeholder_id = "mtcarsrows",
  output_mode = "inline",
  content = { nrow(mtcars) },
  content_type = "text")

map <- knittogether::placeholder_map(
  specs = list(child, plot, inline),
  scalars = list(total = 42)
)

total is a scalar: a plain value passed straight to placeholder_map(). Scalars are quick, but they can only go inline and they don’t carry a description, so the validation log tells you less about them.

as_child = TRUE writes the chunk to its own file in children/ and includes that file, instead of putting the chunk in the main Markdown. Child files run in the same session as the main document, so any data they use must already be loaded. If several child files need the same data, give each one an include of a shared data script, such as {{< include data_processing.qmd >}}.

Fill the placeholders

This example goes straight to the final version, so draft mode and markers are off. For a draft you’ll send back to Word, leave both at their defaults. See “Going back and forth with Word” in vignette("knittogether").

knittogether::replace_placeholders(
  markdown_file = file.path(temp_dir, "example.md"),
  placeholder_prefix = "placeholder_",
  validation_path = file.path(temp_dir, "validation"),
  code_content = map,
  draft_mode = FALSE,
  marker_mode = "off"
)

The end of the Markdown now looks like this:

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.

{{< include children/child_childqmd.qmd >}}

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.

```{r 1x1plot, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=7}
{
    plot(1, 1)
}
```

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.

The number of rows in the data set is `r { nrow(mtcars) }`.

Check the output

Because validation_path was set, the validation/ folder now has a CSV log listing each placeholder, whether it was found, what it was filled with, and whether that changed since the last run. If the quarto and reactable packages are installed there’s also an HTML version you can search and sort.

Render

Include the Markdown in a Quarto document and render it to whatever format you need:

---
format: docx
bibliography: example.bib
---

{{< include example.md >}}

The Quarto document must be in the same folder as example.md, so the include and the child file paths work.

Long documents

A long report can work better as several web pages. split_markdown() splits the Markdown at each top-level heading and writes each section to its own folder, ready for Quarto side navigation:

knittogether::split_markdown(file.path(temp_dir, "example.md"), qmd = "separate")

If you’d rather keep one Markdown file, the quarto-external extension can pull a single section into a page with {{< external example.md#section >}}.
